summary.tldr: Gives First Nations governing bodies control over many lottery schemes on reserves and lets band councils make related bylaws.
what_it_does: Creates authority for a First Nation governing body to run and licence lottery schemes from or on its reserve, after it gives written notice to Canada and the province.
Lets First Nation licences include terms and conditions for how a lottery scheme is run, managed and operated.
Allows charitable and religious groups, fair boards, concession operators and other people to run certain lottery schemes on a reserve under First Nation licences.
Adds a bylaw power in the Indian Act so band councils can regulate lottery schemes allowed under section 207 of the Criminal Code.
Allows computers to be used for ticket sales, winner selection and prize distribution in authorised charitable or religious raffles, including 50/50 draws.
Lets provinces and First Nations agree to sell lottery tickets across provincial and reserve borders for lottery schemes that are already authorised.
summary.background: Section 207 of the Criminal Code already sets out which lottery schemes are lawful. This bill adds First Nation reserve authority to that section and adds a related bylaw power to the Indian Act.
